passages.text: Coronilla minima is a species of flowering plant from the family Fabaceae found in Eastern and Central Spain.

Description 
The plant stems are {{convert|5|-|60|cm}} long and are erect. Leaves grow in 2-4 pairs and are {{convert|0.8|-|2.2|mm}} long and membranous with {{convert|1.2|-|20|mm}} by {{convert|0.8|-|7|mm}} long obovate and spatulate leaflets.

The plant flowers in spring when the Inflorescence carries 4-12 flowers that have a {{convert|1.5|-|3.5|mm}} long peduncle which have ascending {{convert|0.4|mm}} bracteoles and are often deciduous. Pedicels are {{convert|1|-|3.5|mm}} long with {{convert|2|-|4|mm}} long calyx that is glabrous. The Corolla is yellow in colour while the keels that are {{convert|4|-|6.5|mm}} by {{convert|1.5|-|2.1|mm}} have one awn that is {{convert|2|-|2.5|mm}} long. The Fruits are {{convert|10|-|45|mm}} in length and are straight, containing {{convert|1|-|1.1|mm}} by {{convert|3|-|3.8|mm}} transverse to ovoid seeds of a yellowish-brown colour.
